title: Multimodal integration: documents, images, and audio
outcome: Extend the same evidence and validation boundaries to non-text inputs.
cue: New input type. Same questions: source, meaning, permission, evidence.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Extend the same evidence and validation boundaries to non-text inputs.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: A correct transcription can still be interpreted incorrectly. An image can contain instructions intended to redirect the agent. A source location alone does not prove the extracted value is right.

trace.title: Permitted bounded source
trace.detail:
Multimodal models can accept supported combinations of text, images, audio or other inputs. They expand what can be interpreted, not what may be trusted. A scanned form, screenshot or recording can contain missing context, extraction errors or injected instructions.

Preserve provenance through parsing: page, region, timestamp, speaker/segment where relevant, and source version. A document answer may depend on table layout, units, handwriting or an attachment that was not included. Treat OCR/transcription and interpretation as separate stages and evaluate their errors independently.

Bound input size/cost, validate file types with robust handling, control storage/access, and expose uncertain/unreadable states. For important structured values, validate against authoritative records or a human review process. Never silently “correct” a digit because it looks more plausible to the model.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Permitted file → secure bounded parsing → extracted structure with provenance → model interpretation → exact/domain/access checks → reviewed or explicit uncertain result. Test rotated, cropped, blurred, conflicting and malicious-content fixtures.

trace.detail: A correct transcription can still be interpreted incorrectly. An image can contain instructions intended to redirect the agent. A source location alone does not prove the extracted value is right.
